text:
Alex R: Heads up — during the us-west-2 Karpenter rollout a bunch of GPU pods stayed Pending after scale-up. 
Alex R: Pod events show `FailedCreatePodSandBox: failed to allocate ENI` and also `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` in some cases. Trying to collect logs.
Priya S: ugh. that smells like ENI/IP exhaustion + instance-family mismatch. which instance types are allowed in the provisioner? :thinking_face:
Alex R: We were allowing `p4d`, `g5`, and `g4dn` in the same provisioner and had consolidation turned on. here's the provisioner snippet we used:
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family
      operator: In
      values: ["g5", "p4d", "g4dn"]
  consolidation: true
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
```
Priya S: mixing those families can be fine, but g4dn has bad ENI/IP density for heavy pod counts per AZ. if Karpenter favors cheaper/available AZs you'll end up saturating ENIs in one AZ.
Daniel K: agree. we also saw Karpenter launch many smaller GPU instances in the same AZ during our last canary. can we force zone-aware provisioning? e.g. per-AZ provisioners or a `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` requirement.
Maria L: short-term mitigation: disable consolidation and set a soft constraint to spread by zone. also create a tiny warm pool per AZ (tainted) so cold-starts don't force big bursts into a single AZ. :shipit:
oncall
infra-bot: canary-deploy karpenter-provisioner v2 -> started (build 2026-03-16T10:12:03Z)
Alex R: Good call. For the warm pool idea, we can add a provisioner like this (pseudo):
```yaml
spec:
  provider:
    instanceType: [g5.xlarge, g4dn.xlarge]
  limits:
    resources: { cpu: "2000m" } # keep small count
  requirements:
    - key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
      operator: In
      values: [us-west-2a] # create one per AZ
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 86400
  consolidation: false
```
Maria L: also taint the pool `gpu-warm=true:NoSchedule` and add tolerations to the latency-sensitive GPU workloads so they can fall into the pool quickly. less noisy for other jobs.
Daniel K: medium-term: split provisioners by instance-family and AZ, add a `weight` policy if possible, and restrict g4dn to non-primary AZs or lower priority. this reduces large single-AZ pressure.
Priya S: metrics to watch: `eni/allocated_ips`, `eni/available_ips`, `aws_ec2_network_interfaces`, Karpenter Launch/Failure events, and pod Pending reasons. set alerts on ENI free < 20% per AZ.
Alex R: Short-term runbook I'm proposing:
- create 2 tainted warm nodes per AZ (g5.xlarge)
- disable consolidation for 12–24h
- add per-AZ provisioner fallbacks (spot -> on-demand)
- monitor IP metrics and rollback if things worsen

Can someone own the warm pool change and the per-AZ provisioner?
Maria L: I'll take the warm pool + taints. will PR in ~30m. :+1:
Daniel K: I'll work on splitting provisioners by AZ/instance-family and a simple traffic policy to bias away from g4dn until we confirm ENI headroom.
Priya S: I'll add dashboards and an alert rule for ENI usage and pod Pending reasons.
Alex R: thanks. @oncall, if we start seeing user-facing pod failures, please escalate to SRE.
oncall
oncall: noted — will watch the dashboards and be on standby.
Maria L: PR up: k/infra#742 — adds `gpu-warmpool` provisioners (tainted) for us-west-2 a/b/c. includes pod toleration example.
Daniel K: rolled out split provisioners to canary namespace; observing scale events. initial behavior: spots launched more in us-west-2a, but ENI pressure reduced 15% after warm nodes. :eyes:
Alex R: nice, let's keep consolidation disabled for 24h and regroup after 48h of monitoring. thanks all. :pray:
